summary_text: Ñuble registered a +300 % increase in recorded homo/transphobic cases in 2024, the sharpest percentage rise of any Chilean region, though from an extremely small base: Ñuble held only 1.44 % of the national case total. La Discusión's reporting of two historic gender-identity rectification cases in Ñuble illustrates how minimal the formal trans presence is in the region. The statistical alarm is real — the fastest percentage growth in the country — but the absolute numbers remain marginal, and no region-specific legal finding, institutional incident, or enforcement failure was identified in the dossier beyond the case-volume trend. A 2026 follow-up in the same paper reports homo/transphobic attacks rising a further 16.6 % in Ñuble in 2025. Against the national 0.72, this is a −0.05 deviation, driven entirely by the rate-of-change signal. Compared with Bío-Bío (0.62), which is 0.05 lower, Ñuble lacks the hospital bed-placement and diversity-office-dismantling findings that give Bío-Bío a concrete traveler-facing institutional failure. Ñuble's evidence is statistical trajectory without a named incident. Compared with La Araucanía (0.65), Ñuble is 0.02 higher: Araucanía's +150 % is in the most recent year (2025) and is accompanied by the lowest gender-identity-law uptake of any region (157 in three years), painting a more sustained picture of emerging hostility with no institutional counterweight.

sources.title: Derechos LGBTIQ+ retroceden por primera vez en democracia y los casos y denuncias por homo/transfobia aumentan un 78% en Chile – Movilh Chile
sources.claim_summary: Movilh press release of the XXIII Annual Human-Rights Report on Sexual and Gender Diversity (18 March 2025): homo/transphobia cases rose 78.7 % to 2,847 in 2024 — 23.5 % of all cases recorded in 23 years — the first regression of LGBTIQ+ rights since the return of democracy, with roll-backs in all three branches of state; police-space assaults +200 %, hate speech +116.9 %, hate campaigns +80 %, institutional discrimination +63.9 %, media abuses +50 %, while hate killings fell 33.3 %. Trans people made up 39.73 % of 2024 cases (1,131, up 462.69 % year-on-year). The full report's per-region series places Ñuble first nationally on rate of increase (+300 %) from a marginal 1.44 % share of the national total.

sources.title: Más de 12 mil personas han cambiado su nombre y sexo legal en Chile: La historia de dos casos históricos en Ñuble – La Discusión
sources.claim_summary: La Discusión (the Ñuble regional daily, Chillán; 11 July 2026) on 12,669 people having rectified name and legal sex nationally under the eight-year-old Gender Identity Law (64.6 % trans men, 35.1 % trans women, 42 non-binary/intersex 'X' registrations, per Registry data obtained by Movilh): the article tells Ñuble's two historic cases — Pascal Roma Irribarra Cisternas, subject of the region's first court ruling granting a non-binary adult's birth-certificate rectification (First Civil Court of Chillán), and teacher Alexander 'Alex' Villarroel Muñoz, among Ñuble's first trans men to complete the legal change (new ID from 3 February 2020), who underwent hormones in Concepción/Chillán and waits for surgery. Both recount hostile institutional episodes (a school director's remarks blocking Pascal's teaching hire; a secret faculty meeting over Alex's social name at a conservative university); Registry officials declined to release Ñuble-level figures, deferring to national level — underscoring how small the registered trans population is in the region.
